title: The Widening Gap
text:
Economic inequality has widened in many industrialized countries over the past four decades. Researchers attribute this trend partly to technological change, which has increased demand for highly skilled workers, and partly to the decline of union membership. Although overall national income has grown, the gains have been concentrated among the wealthiest households. As a result, many middle-income families report that their living standards have stagnated.

Economists disagree, however, about the most effective remedies. Some advocate progressive taxation and expanded public education, arguing that these measures redistribute opportunity as well as income. Others contend that excessive regulation discourages investment and ultimately harms the very groups it intends to protect. Whatever the policy preference, most analysts agree that inequality is no longer a marginal concern but a central issue of public debate.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what has increased demand for highly skilled workers?
According to paragraph two, what do some economists advocate?
options: Progressive taxation and expanded public education

questions.text: What can be inferred about middle-income families from the first paragraph?
options: They have benefited most from recent growth
Their living standards have not kept pace with overall national income
They are unaffected by technological change

questions.text: What is the author's most likely view of economic inequality?
options: It has been solved by recent policies
It has become a central issue that requires attention
It is caused only by individual choices

paragraph_translations: La desigualdad económica se ha ampliado en muchos países industrializados durante las últimas cuatro décadas. Los investigadores atribuyen esta tendencia en parte al cambio tecnológico, que ha aumentado la demanda de trabajadores altamente cualificados, y en parte a la disminución de la afiliación sindical. Aunque el ingreso nacional total ha crecido, las ganancias se han concentrado entre los hogares más ricos. Como resultado, muchas familias de ingresos medios afirman que su nivel de vida se ha estancado.

Sin embargo, los economistas no están de acuerdo sobre los remedios más eficaces. Algunos defienden los impuestos progresivos y la ampliación de la educación pública, argumentando que estas medidas redistribuyen la oportunidad además del ingreso. Otros sostienen que la regulación excesiva desalienta la inversión y, en última instancia, perjudica a los mismos grupos que pretende proteger. Cualquiera que sea la preferencia política, la mayoría de los analistas coinciden en que la desigualdad ya no es una preocupación marginal, sino un tema central del debate público.
